newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTANI SPECTATORS STONE OWN TEAM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTANI SPECTATORS STONE OWN TEAM.

text.p: Spectators, angered
by Pakistan's failure to bowl out Zimbabwe on Friday, stoned
their own team in the opening session of the second day of the
first test.
Although no injuries were reported, lunch was taken five
minutes early at the Sheikhupura ground, a new test venue.
At the interval Zimbabwe, who resumed at 240 for six in
their first innings, were 371 for nine.
Grant Flower and Paul Strang both struck excellent centuries
as the Zimbabwe batsman continued to defy the Pakistan bowlers.
Opener Flower, 98 overnight, completed the second test
hundred of his career by driving paceman Shahid Nazir for his
12th four.
He eventually fell for 110 to off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq
having added a Zimbabwe record 131 runs for the seventh wicket
with Strang.
Strang, not out 37, reached his maiden test century by
taking two runs off Wasim Akram after the Pakistani captain had
taken the second new ball in the 103rd over.
Strang, playing his 10th test, was twice dropped by Shadab
Kabir off Waqar Younis on his way to his century, which he
reached in 301 minutes with the help of nine fours.
He put on 87 runs with his brother Bryan, erasing Zimbabwe's
previous best ninth-wicket partnership of 40.
Bryan Strang had made 42 when he was clean bowled by
Saqlain. Zimbabwe's total was their highest ever in Pakistan,
beating the 289 they scored in Karachi in the 1993-94 series.
